+B1 adds `resolveWalletCredential(tx, { subject, walletNetworks })` and `revokeWalletCredential(tx, { subject, walletNetworks, accountId, actorAccountId, requestId, session, now })` without new schema or app routes. Both require the existing injected READ COMMITTED transaction. Approved networks and trusted session/clock observations come from the composing host; they are not HTTP assertions.
+
+`resolveWalletCredential` returns `{ source: 'ABSENT' }` or internal `{ source: 'PRIMARY' | 'LINK', accountId, participantId, linkId, address, networkIdentity }`. This is **transaction-bound ownership context**, not authentication or a portable session authorization. A host must verify a fresh sign-in proof independently, resolve and create a session inside the same still-live transaction, using the documented locks. Never cache or expose account/participant/link IDs publicly. A legitimate legacy PRIMARY may have `participantId: null` and never provisions a mapping on sign-in. A LINK must match its account's existing immutable HUMAN participant; revoked links, restricted owners, unsupported networks and malformed durable observations fail closed. An ABSENT observation authorizes no user creation; that remains host-owned legacy behavior, not a B1 command.
+
+`revokeWalletCredential` requires an active unexpired self-session from the trusted host, actor equality and an unsuspended account. It locks subject then account, validates immutable mapping and changes only ACTIVE→REVOKED with the injected timestamp. It returns internal `{ outcome: 'REVOKED' | 'ALREADY_REVOKED', linkId, participantId, address, networkIdentity, status: 'REVOKED', revokedAt }`. Repeating preserves the original revokedAt. A missing or foreign target returns the same sanitized IDENTITY_CONFLICT; an own primary returns PRIMARY_WALLET_PROTECTED. Existing rows and provenance remain, and an address remains reserved without automatic reactivation. Request identity is accepted for host audit composition; B1 does not persist a revocation receipt or audit event. Before any non-test acknowledgement, the composing host must durably audit and invalidate sessions in this same transaction; B2 must review the all-session versus credential-attribution choice. +## Wallet sign-in session authority (T007 AC02 precursor, internal v1)
+
+Purpose: decide which authority (`wallet` or `x`) the replacement session receives when a wallet sign-in or link is verified while the caller already holds a session. +- An expired X session no longer renews X authority through a wallet signature.
+- A cookie session owned by another account is neither deleted nor borrowed.
+- Folding the signed-in X account into the wallet owner yields a `wallet` session.

 This directory declares its own dependencies (`package.json`), a minimal `User`/`WalletIdentity`/`Participant`/`WalletLink` schema and its own four migrations (host-owned `User` and `WalletIdentity` tables, plus the exact participant-mapping and wallet-link migrations as symlinks to the canonical SQL). `contracts`, `identity`, `identity-storage`, `identity-link`, `lib/identity-storage-adapter.ts` and `lib/wallet-link-proof.ts` are symlinks to the canonical sources; copy with `cp -RL` so the copy is self-contained. Supply `DATABASE_URL` for a disposable local database yourself; the host refuses non-local URLs and `NODE_ENV=production`. It never imports RAID configuration or `src/lib/db`.

Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **E01-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **E01-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **E01-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **E01-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **E01-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **E01-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **E01-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **E01-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **E01-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **E01-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **E01-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **E01-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **E01-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n\n- [ ] **E01-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **E01-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **E01-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **E01-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI matrix](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-ci-plan.md)\n\n### Systems and subsection contracts\n\n- [00.1 — What this file is Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **E05-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **E05-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **E05-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **E05-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **E05-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **E05-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **E05-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **E05-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n\n- [ ] **E05-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **E05-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **E05-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **E10-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **E10-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **E10-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **E10-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **E10-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **E10-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **E10-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **E10-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **E10-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **E10-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n\n- [ ] **E10-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **E10-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **E10-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **E10-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **E20-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **E20-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. 216 subsections, R/P/D/I/AC/O/G groups, native epics/children and evidence register.\n\n**Permission contract:** Product owner controls recorded policy; domain owners implement bounded contracts; independent reviewers verify evidence; no agent may manufacture approvals.\n\n**State/effect contract:** Track actual NOT_STARTED/IN_PROGRESS/IMPLEMENTED_UNVERIFIED/VERIFIED_IN_TEST/PILOT_ENABLED/PRODUCTION_ENABLED evidence; project fields are planning until proven.\n\n**Adverse/recovery cases:** Missing subsection/requirement owner; closed child with no evidence; removed criterion; weaker assertion; unresolved production gate; claimed complete product with unimplemented domain.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.\n\n- [ ] **E23-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **E23-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **E23-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **E23-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **E23-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **E23-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **E23-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **E23-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **E23-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **E23-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **E23-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **E23-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **E23-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **E23-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **E23-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **E23-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **E23-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **E23-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n\n- [ ] **E23-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **E23-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **E23-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **E23-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI matrix](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-ci-plan.md)\n\n### Systems and subsection contracts\n\nAll 258 sections/subsections are individually indexed in the master epic table above and the [complete system map](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-blueprint-project-map.md). For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **O04-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **O04-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **O04-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **O04-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **O04-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **O04-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **O04-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **O04-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **O04-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. client signatures alone prove no funding.\n\n**State/effect contract:** Agreement/funding/claim/attempt states separate; verified credit bounds paid+refunded+remaining per asset; protected committed reserves cannot be withdrawn as uncommitted funds.\n\n**Adverse/recovery cases:** Partial multi-asset deposit; same ticker different mint; refund/binding race; duplicate webhook; rebuilt claim signature; frozen transfer; partial Party payout; asset-policy change.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. Source requirements prevail; refresh this packet if the canonical contract changes.\n\n### Exact applicable requirements and scenarios\n\n| ID | Authority class | Required behavior | Qualification / expected result |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| I03 | INVARIANT | Every financial obligation and transfer uses integer base units and a full asset identity. |  |\n| I04 | INVARIANT | Cumulative paid, refunded, and remaining obligations never exceed verified credited funds for that asset. |  |\n| I05 | INVARIANT | A duplicate command, webhook, retry, or reconciliation pass cannot create a duplicate business outcome. |  |\n| I08 | INVARIANT | Every acceptance and financial decision refers to immutable terms and a specific submission/version. |  |\n| I09 | INVARIANT | External effects are recorded, retried, and reconciled; a database transaction cannot pretend to atomically commit GitHub and Solana. |  |\n| I10 | INVARIANT | Only authorized actors can change the underlying business state; hiding a button is not authorization. |  |\n| I11 | INVARIANT | Payout, refund, access grant, and dispute decisions have an audit trail and explicit authority. |  |\n| I12 | INVARIANT | Sample program IDs, fake mints, and fabricated performance data cannot pass production validation. |  |\n| P05 | DIRECTION | Rewards can combine supported stablecoins, SOL, project tokens, and RAID. | Support follows tested adapters; “anything” is not unchecked arbitrary-token acceptance. |\n\n### Explicit domain binding — Escrow, assets and settlement\n\n**Affected canonical records:** assets, reward_obligations, escrow_agreements, funding_observations, settlement_allocations, claims, ledger_entries, chain_operations, transaction_attempts.\n\n**Permission contract:** Funder, allowed beneficiaries, allocation authority and claim authority follow accepted terms and chosen escrow contract; client signatures alone prove no funding.\n\n**State/effect contract:** Agreement/funding/claim/attempt states separate; verified credit bounds paid+refunded+remaining per asset; protected committed reserves cannot be withdrawn as uncommitted funds.\n\n**Adverse/recovery cases:** Partial multi-asset deposit; same ticker different mint; refund/binding race; duplicate webhook; rebuilt claim signature; frozen transfer; partial Party payout; asset-policy change.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.\n\n- [ ] **O08-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **O08-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **O08-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **O08-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **O08-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **O08-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **O08-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **O08-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **O08-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **O08-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **O08-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **O08-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **O08-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **O08-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **O08-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **O08-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **O08-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **O08-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **O08-A01 (task acceptance)**: Accepted decision names exact policy/authority and evidence.\n- [ ] **O08-A02 (task acceptance)**: Dependent feature stays disabled while unresolved; independent interfaces may proceed.\n- [ ] **O08-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Prepare concrete options and affected dependencies.\n- [ ] **O08-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Evaluate authority, money, privacy, provider and migration consequences.\n- [ ] **O08-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Record owner/date/status, exact adopted values, rationale and rejected alternatives using blueprint section 40.4.\n- [ ] **O08-W04 (implementation outcome)**: Update O08 in the canonical blueprint and dependent contracts/tests together after the owner accepts a choice.\n\n- [ ] **O08-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **O08-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **O08-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **O08-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI client signatures alone prove no funding.\n\n**State/effect contract:** Agreement/funding/claim/attempt states separate; verified credit bounds paid+refunded+remaining per asset; protected committed reserves cannot be withdrawn as uncommitted funds.\n\n**Adverse/recovery cases:** Partial multi-asset deposit; same ticker different mint; refund/binding race; duplicate webhook; rebuilt claim signature; frozen transfer; partial Party payout; asset-policy change.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.\n\n- [ ] **O14-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **O14-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **O14-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **O14-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **O14-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **O14-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **O14-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **O14-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **O14-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **O14-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **O14-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **O14-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **O14-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **O14-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **O14-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **O14-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **O14-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **O14-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **O14-A01 (task acceptance)**: Accepted decision names exact policy/authority and evidence.\n- [ ] **O14-A02 (task acceptance)**: Dependent feature stays disabled while unresolved; independent interfaces may proceed.\n- [ ] **O14-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Prepare concrete options and affected dependencies.\n- [ ] **O14-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Evaluate authority, money, privacy, provider and migration consequences.\n- [ ] **O14-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Record owner/date/status, exact adopted values, rationale and rejected alternatives using blueprint section 40.4.\n- [ ] **O14-W04 (implementation outcome)**: Update O14 in the canonical blueprint and dependent contracts/tests together after the owner accepts a choice.\n\n- [ ] **O14-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **O14-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **O14-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **O14-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI matrix](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-ci-plan.md)\n\n### Systems and subsection contracts\n\n- [02.1 — Locked product named case/release owner; audited configuration changes; no arbitrary force-paid or erase-history action.\n\n**State/effect contract:** Flags block new server commands while preserving old claims/reconciliation; backup/restore recovers terms/consents/semantic IDs/capacity before writes resume.\n\n**Adverse/recovery cases:** Worker crash; lost snapshot interval; repeated outbox/inbox; failed provider; stale grant job; unavailable safe recovery; rollback after irreversible external effect.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements.
