Source requirements prevail; refresh this packet if the canonical contract changes.\n\n### Exact applicable requirements and scenarios\n\n| ID | Authority class | Required behavior | Qualification / expected result |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| I01 | INVARIANT | The database rejects a second active engagement for the same canonical participant. |  |\n| I02 | INVARIANT | Party activation either reserves every participant or reserves none. |  |\n| I03 | INVARIANT | Every financial obligation and transfer uses integer base units and a full asset identity. |  |\n| I04 | INVARIANT | Cumulative paid, refunded, and remaining obligations never exceed verified credited funds for that asset. |  |\n| I05 | INVARIANT | A duplicate command, webhook, retry, or reconciliation pass cannot create a duplicate business outcome. |  |\n| I06 | INVARIANT | Private bytes never appear in public API fields, rendered page payloads, search indexes, previews, logs, or notification snippets. |  |\n| I07 | INVARIANT | No background score change, token sale, or service outage grants code access or confiscates a reward. |  |\n| I08 | INVARIANT | Every acceptance and financial decision refers to immutable terms and a specific submission/version. |  |\n| I09 | INVARIANT | External effects are recorded, retried, and reconciled; a database transaction cannot pretend to atomically commit GitHub and Solana. |  |\n| I10 | INVARIANT | Only authorized actors can change the underlying business state; hiding a button is not authorization. |  |\n| I11 | INVARIANT | Payout, refund, access grant, and dispute decisions have an audit trail and explicit authority. |  |\n| I12 | INVARIANT | Sample program IDs, fake mints, and fabricated performance data cannot pass production validation. |  |\n| R01 | LOCKED | RAID retains a project launchpad and Guild identity. | C01 |\n| R02 | LOCKED | A project launched through RAID becomes a Guild; its authorized creator becomes the Guild Founder. | C01, C04 |\n| R03 | LOCKED | Holding the recognized project token establishes holder eligibility for that Guild. | C04 |\n| R04 | LOCKED | A Raider can work across Guilds and can also be a Founder or Member. | C01, C04 |\n| R05 | LOCKED | Every published Raid has an E–S difficulty label and explicit skill requirements. | C01, C02, C05 |\n| R06 | LOCKED | Skill rank represents demonstrated capacity, not token wealth or paid placement. | C05 |\n| R07 | LOCKED | RAID recommends task difficulty and reward composition/range; participant routing and duration complete the proposed assistance flow. | C02 directly requests rank/reward; routing/duration are carried-forward additions |\n| R08 | LOCKED | The public website has a discoverable Raid feed. | C03 |\n| R09 | LOCKED | Paid placement exists as a clearly distinguishable visibility product. | C03; labeling is a trust-preserving implementation requirement |\n| R10 | LOCKED | Guilds accumulate a reputation based on funding, payment, requirements, and treatment of contributors. | C06 |\n| R11 | LOCKED | Sensitive work uses progressive trust and explicit access approval. | C07, C08 |\n| R12 | LOCKED | Skills can be claimed, evidenced, assessed, and verified independently. | C08 |\n| R13 | LOCKED | One Raider may hold only one active Raid/work engagement at a time. | C09 |\n| R14 | LOCKED | A high-trust Challenge may select a Raider or Party for a larger Raid. | C10 |\n\n### Explicit domain binding — Shared contracts and architecture\n\n**Affected canonical records:** accounts, participants, terms_versions, engagements, active_commitments, assets, command_receipts, outbox_events, audit_events.\n\n**Permission contract:** Domain owners define commands; operations have scoped repair authority; development access does not imply customer or treasury authority.\n\n**State/effect contract:** Additive migration/backfill; immutable terms and semantic IDs survive rollback/restore; constraints and outbox are established before dependent slices.\n\n**Adverse/recovery cases:** Legacy obligations survive migration; crash after external success; restore with missing recent acceptance; same idempotency key with altered request.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.\n\n- [ ] **T001-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **T001-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **T001-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **T001-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **T001-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **T001-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **T001-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **T001-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **T001-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **T001-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T001-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T001-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T001-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T001-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T001-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **T001-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **T001-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **T001-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **T001-A01 (task acceptance)**: Inventory links to actual files and evidence, not assumed completion\n- [ ] **T001-A02 (task acceptance)**: New policies have a documented compatibility path for old commitments\n- [ ] **T001-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Inspect source, schema, migrations, CI, flags and prior results\n- [ ] **T001-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Record equivalent implementations and gaps for participant/Guild/terms/work/money/access\n- [ ] **T001-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Identify existing paid obligations and frozen campaign policy versions\n\n- [ ] **T001-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T001-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T001-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T001-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI constraints and outbox are established before dependent slices.\n\n**Adverse/recovery cases:** Legacy obligations survive migration; crash after external success; restore with missing recent acceptance; same idempotency key with altered request.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.\n\n- [ ] **T002-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **T002-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **T002-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **T002-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **T002-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **T002-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **T002-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **T002-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **T002-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **T002-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T002-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T002-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T002-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T002-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T002-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **T002-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **T002-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **T002-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **T002-A01 (task acceptance)**: Consumers use one contract source\n- [ ] **T002-A02 (task acceptance)**: Work, money, access, dispute and transaction states remain distinct\n- [ ] **T002-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Define canonical identity, Guild, terms, engagement, asset and exact amount contracts\n- [ ] **T002-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Assign each state transition and authority to one command owner\n- [ ] **T002-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Record API versioning, error envelopes and global lock order\n\n- [ ] **T002-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T002-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T002-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T002-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI matrix](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-ci-plan.md)\n\n### Systems and subsection contracts\n\n- [00 — Agent entry operations have scoped repair authority; development access does not imply customer or treasury authority.\n\n**State/effect contract:** Additive migration/backfill; immutable terms and semantic IDs survive rollback/restore; constraints and outbox are established before dependent slices.\n\n**Adverse/recovery cases:** Legacy obligations survive migration; crash after external success; restore with missing recent acceptance; same idempotency key with altered request.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T002-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **T003-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **T003-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **T003-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **T003-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **T003-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **T003-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T003-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T003-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T003-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T003-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T003-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **T003-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **T003-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **T003-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **T003-A01 (task acceptance)**: Migration plan names affected tables and checks\n- [ ] **T003-A02 (task acceptance)**: Applied migrations remain immutable\n- [ ] **T003-W01 (implementation outcome)**: List schema additions and backfills\n- [ ] **T003-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Explain how accepted history and financial records remain valid\n- [ ] **T003-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Define verification and honest rollback boundaries\n\n- [ ] **T003-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T003-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T003-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T003-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI matrix](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-ci-plan.md)\n\n### Systems and subsection contracts\n\n- [00.1 — What this file is See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T004-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T004-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI Use the [feature/integration matrix and documentation contract](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-module-reuse.md). Demonstrate an independent consuming host and meaningful contract tests; never treat authentication, storage or authorization as an undocumented RAID-global singleton. Preserve canonical identity/history/capacity/claims across swaps.\n\n### Evidence and approval record required before Done\n\nFor each criterion attach canonical reference, affected real files/entities, permitted/rejected actors, before/after state, test setup/action/expected result, observed result, command/report URL, SHA, environment/provider version, reviewer and disposition. Record OPEN decisions and applicable G01–G10 separately. UAT needs representative execution and business sign-off; a development agent cannot fabricate this approval.\n\nHard dependencies must have reviewed evidence, not merely closed issue status. Failed criteria remain visible with defect/retest links. Scope moved to another issue stays linked and blocks its dependent outcome. Preserve customer terms and financial/access history. a database transaction cannot pretend to atomically commit GitHub and Solana. |  |\n| I10 | INVARIANT | Only authorized actors can change the underlying business state; hiding a button is not authorization. |  |\n| I11 | INVARIANT | Payout, refund, access grant, and dispute decisions have an audit trail and explicit authority. |  |\n| I12 | INVARIANT | Sample program IDs, fake mints, and fabricated performance data cannot pass production validation. |  |\n\n### Explicit domain binding — Operations, administration and recovery\n\n**Affected canonical records:** configuration_versions, audit_events, outbox_events, webhook_inbox, job_attempts, command_receipts.\n\n**Permission contract:** Scoped support/access/finance/product permissions; named case/release owner; audited configuration changes; no arbitrary force-paid or erase-history action.\n\n**State/effect contract:** Flags block new server commands while preserving old claims/reconciliation; backup/restore recovers terms/consents/semantic IDs/capacity before writes resume.\n\n**Adverse/recovery cases:** Worker crash; lost snapshot interval; repeated outbox/inbox; failed provider; stale grant job; unavailable safe recovery; rollback after irreversible external effect.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **T005-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **T005-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **T005-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **T005-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **T005-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **T005-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T005-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T005-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T005-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T005-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T005-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.\n\n- [ ] **T012-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **T012-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **T012-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **T012-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **T012-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **T012-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **T012-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **T012-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **T012-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **T012-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T012-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T012-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T012-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T012-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T012-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **T012-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **T012-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **T012-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **T012-A01 (task acceptance)**: Wallet/token wealth never creates a verified rank\n- [ ] **T012-A02 (task acceptance)**: One verified frontend skill cannot satisfy Solana requirements\n- [ ] **T012-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Create stable skill IDs/aliases\n- [ ] **T012-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Store claim, verification state, rubric/version, evidence, evaluator and confidence\n- [ ] **T012-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Preserve reassessment/revocation history\n\n- [ ] **T012-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T012-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T012-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T012-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **T024-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **T024-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **T024-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **T024-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **T024-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **T024-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T024-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T024-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T024-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T024-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T024-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **T024-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **T024-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **T024-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **T024-A01 (task acceptance)**: Late cleanup cannot release a newer job\n- [ ] **T024-A02 (task acceptance)**: Payment pending does not consume terminal work capacity\n- [ ] **T024-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Implement finite setup/build/review/revision deadlines\n- [ ] **T024-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Close work and release matching participant+engagement atomically\n- [ ] **T024-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Preserve unpaid claims/evidence and require consent/capacity to reopen\n\n- [ ] **T024-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T024-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T024-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T024-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI Material amendment needs affected consent, required additional funding and a new audited version; unilateral overwrite is rejected. |\n| I05 | INVARIANT | A duplicate command, webhook, retry, or reconciliation pass cannot create a duplicate business outcome. |  |\n| I08 | INVARIANT | Every acceptance and financial decision refers to immutable terms and a specific submission/version. |  |\n| I10 | INVARIANT | Only authorized actors can change the underlying business state; hiding a button is not authorization. |  |\n| R04 | LOCKED | A Raider can work across Guilds and can also be a Founder or Member. | C01, C04 |\n| R13 | LOCKED | One Raider may hold only one active Raid/work engagement at a time. | C09 |\n\n### Explicit domain binding — Delivery, review and bounded closure\n\n**Affected canonical records:** submissions, reviews, engagements, terms_versions, disputes, active_commitments.\n\n**Permission contract:** Assigned executor submits own exact version; separately authorized reviewer decides against accepted criteria; no self-approval or unilateral rewrite.\n\n**State/effect contract:** IN_PROGRESS/SUBMITTED/UNDER_REVIEW/REVISION_REQUESTED retain capacity; terminal operational outcome releases matching engagement independently of money.\n\n**Adverse/recovery cases:** Silent reviewer; no submission; revision duty; payment pending after acceptance; replacement; attempted reopening while worker already has new engagement.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.\n\n- [ ] **T025-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **T025-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **T025-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **T025-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **T025-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **T025-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **T025-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **T025-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **T025-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **T025-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T025-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T025-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T025-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T025-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T025-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **T025-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **T025-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **T025-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **T025-A01 (task acceptance)**: Unilateral founder/admin/default changes rejected\n- [ ] **T025-A02 (task acceptance)**: Replacement records new obligation rather than deleting old contribution\n- [ ] **T025-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Version scope/reward/deadline changes with affected consent\n- [ ] **T025-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Verify additional funding and capacity when required\n- [ ] **T025-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Retain original accepted history and clear amendment audit\n\n- [ ] **T025-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T025-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T025-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T026-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T026-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path.
