Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.\n\n- [ ] **T030-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **T030-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **T030-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **T030-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **T030-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **T030-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **T030-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **T030-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **T030-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **T030-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T030-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T030-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T030-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T030-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T030-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **T030-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **T030-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **T030-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **T030-A01 (task acceptance)**: Founder cannot refund bound work unilaterally\n- [ ] **T030-A02 (task acceptance)**: No model/admin generic arbitrary-withdrawal power\n- [ ] **T030-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Compare existing custody to O05 authority model\n- [ ] **T030-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Record permitted signers/beneficiaries/upgrade and termination paths\n- [ ] **T030-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Demonstrate binding/refund/claim replay protection in selected environment\n\n- [ ] **T030-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T030-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T030-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T030-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI matrix](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-ci-plan.md)\n\n### Systems and subsection contracts\n\n- [13.1 — Exact product Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **T032-A01 (task acceptance)**: Refund-winning race closes unstarted work cleanly\n- [ ] **T032-A02 (task acceptance)**: Late binding cannot restart work or auto-grant code\n- [ ] **T032-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Persist semantic binding intent after atomic acceptance\n- [ ] **T032-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Verify chain/provider terms/roster/beneficiaries\n- [ ] **T032-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Recheck generation and readiness before StartEngagement; compensate late success after closure\n\n- [ ] **T032-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T032-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T032-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T032-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. same ticker different mint; refund/binding race; duplicate webhook; rebuilt claim signature; frozen transfer; partial Party payout; asset-policy change.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.\n\n- [ ] **T032-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **T032-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **T032-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **T032-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **T032-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **T032-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **T032-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **T032-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **T032-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **T032-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T032-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T032-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T032-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T032-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T032-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **T032-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **T032-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **T032-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **T032-A01 (task acceptance)**: Refund-winning race closes unstarted work cleanly\n- [ ] **T032-A02 (task acceptance)**: Late binding cannot restart work or auto-grant code\n- [ ] **T032-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Persist semantic binding intent after atomic acceptance\n- [ ] **T032-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Verify chain/provider terms/roster/beneficiaries\n- [ ] **T032-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Recheck generation and readiness before StartEngagement; compensate late success after closure\n\n- [ ] **T032-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T032-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T032-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T032-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI matrix](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-ci-plan.md)\n\n### Systems and subsection contracts\n\n- [13 — One active Blueprint source SHA-256: `cbd982db21e317305617f6068f8ded3b02689ffa15b8ca21ccc9221ab8fde7ef`. Source requirements prevail; refresh this packet if the canonical contract changes.\n\n### Exact applicable requirements and scenarios\n\n| ID | Authority class | Required behavior | Qualification / expected result |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| D01 | DEFAULT | One TypeScript modular monolith, PostgreSQL, web process, background worker, and separate untrusted execution environments. | Keeps transactions and ownership clear without early microservices. |\n| D12 | DEFAULT | Mainnet payments and trading remain disabled until their specific implementation and operating gates pass. | A mock or devnet flow is not a production payment system. |\n| I05 | INVARIANT | A duplicate command, webhook, retry, or reconciliation pass cannot create a duplicate business outcome. |  |\n| I06 | INVARIANT | Private bytes never appear in public API fields, rendered page payloads, search indexes, previews, logs, or notification snippets. |  |\n| I09 | INVARIANT | External effects are recorded, retried, and reconciled; a database transaction cannot pretend to atomically commit GitHub and Solana. |  |\n| I10 | INVARIANT | Only authorized actors can change the underlying business state; hiding a button is not authorization. |  |\n| I11 | INVARIANT | Payout, refund, access grant, and dispute decisions have an audit trail and explicit authority. |  |\n| I12 | INVARIANT | Sample program IDs, fake mints, and fabricated performance data cannot pass production validation. |  |\n\n### Explicit domain binding — Operations, administration and recovery\n\n**Affected canonical records:** configuration_versions, audit_events, outbox_events, webhook_inbox, job_attempts, command_receipts.\n\n**Permission contract:** Scoped support/access/finance/product permissions; named case/release owner; audited configuration changes; no arbitrary force-paid or erase-history action.\n\n**State/effect contract:** Flags block new server commands while preserving old claims/reconciliation; backup/restore recovers terms/consents/semantic IDs/capacity before writes resume.\n\n**Adverse/recovery cases:** Worker crash; lost snapshot interval; repeated outbox/inbox; failed provider; stale grant job; unavailable safe recovery; rollback after irreversible external effect.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.\n\n- [ ] **T040-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **T040-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **T040-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **T040-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **T040-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **T040-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **T040-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T040-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T040-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T040-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T040-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T040-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **T040-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T047-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **T055-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T055-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T055-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T055-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T055-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T055-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **T055-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **T055-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **T055-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **T055-A01 (task acceptance)**: Stale grant job cannot revive access\n- [ ] **T055-A02 (task acceptance)**: Failed provider revoke stays visible; copied data is not claimed recalled\n- [ ] **T055-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Revoke secrets and reconcile desired/effective access\n- [ ] **T055-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Retry failures with explicit incident owner\n- [ ] **T055-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Execute untrusted code/URLs only inside approved boundary and reject prompt/tool authority injection\n\n- [ ] **T055-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T055-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T055-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T055-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.\n\n- [ ] **T062-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **T062-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **T062-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **T062-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **T062-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **T062-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **T062-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **T062-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **T062-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **T062-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T062-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T062-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T062-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T062-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T062-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **T062-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **T062-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **T062-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **T062-A01 (task acceptance)**: Two operator jobs conflict\n- [ ] **T062-A02 (task acceptance)**: Same allowed Party members share one operator reservation\n- [ ] **T062-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Count distinct engagements for individual pilot operator\n- [ ] **T062-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Include own human duty and allow same-engagement Party sharing\n- [ ] **T062-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Lock operator and participant reservations atomically in every accept/handoff path\n\n- [ ] **T062-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T062-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T062-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T062-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI matrix](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-ci-plan.md)\n\n### Systems and subsection contracts\n\n- [07.1 — Account failed cancellation cannot strand capacity.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.\n\n- [ ] **T064-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **T064-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **T064-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **T064-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **T064-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **T064-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **T064-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **T064-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **T064-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **T064-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T064-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T064-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T064-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T064-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T064-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **T064-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **T064-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **T064-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **T064-A01 (task acceptance)**: Model cannot raise its own cap\n- [ ] **T064-A02 (task acceptance)**: Compute budget cannot consume contributor reward reserves\n- [ ] **T064-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Track actual/estimated cost with currency/rate-card version\n- [ ] **T064-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Reserve total cap across model/tools/retries/subcalls\n- [ ] **T064-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Stop/pause at cap and follow disclosed unused-budget/partial-result policy\n\n- [ ] **T064-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T064-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T064-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T064-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI matrix](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-ci-plan.md)\n\n### Systems and subsection contracts\n\n- [07.1 — Account Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T072-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T072-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T072-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **T072-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **T072-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **T072-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **T072-A01 (task acceptance)**: Token wealth cannot change skill/reliability\n- [ ] **T072-A02 (task acceptance)**: Nonwinner and unresolved allegation are not automatic failure\n- [ ] **T072-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Adopt O09 formula/rubric and sample-confidence policy\n- [ ] **T072-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Review related-party and false-positive signals\n- [ ] **T072-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Version corrections and reassessment without erasing attributable history\n\n- [ ] **T072-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T072-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T072-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T072-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. source grant removal preserves valid target grant.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale.
