no private bytes. |\n| AC43 | ACCEPTANCE | High-rank token holder requests a repo without approval. | No automatic grant. |\n| AC44 | ACCEPTANCE | Founder grants one repository expecting folder secrecy. | UI/config identifies actual scope; approved isolated resource required. |\n| AC45 | ACCEPTANCE | Source Challenge grant is revoked after main-Raid grant starts on same repo. | Effective reconciliation preserves the new valid access. |\n| AC46 | ACCEPTANCE | Contributor had independent repository rights before the Raid. | Removing RAID grant does not claim all access disappeared or delete unrelated rights. |\n| AC47 | ACCEPTANCE | Provider revocation fails or old grant job arrives late. | Incident/retry; stale grant cannot revive undesired access. |\n| AC48 | ACCEPTANCE | Submission includes a malicious build script, URL, or prompt instruction. | Isolation/input policy prevents unauthorized data or tool access. |\n| AC49 | ACCEPTANCE | Account is restricted with an unsettled claim. | Safe access to financial status and dispute evidence remains under policy. |\n| I06 | INVARIANT | Private bytes never appear in public API fields, rendered page payloads, search indexes, previews, logs, or notification snippets. |  |\n| I07 | INVARIANT | No background score change, token sale, or service outage grants code access or confiscates a reward. |  |\n| I09 | INVARIANT | External effects are recorded, retried, and reconciled; a database transaction cannot pretend to atomically commit GitHub and Solana. |  |\n| I10 | INVARIANT | Only authorized actors can change the underlying business state; hiding a button is not authorization. |  |\n| I11 | INVARIANT | Payout, refund, access grant, and dispute decisions have an audit trail and explicit authority. |  |\n| R11 | LOCKED | Sensitive work uses progressive trust and explicit access approval. | C07, C08 |\n\n### Explicit domain binding — Private resources and effective grants\n\n**Affected canonical records:** raid_private_briefs, resources, access_grants, engagement_members, audit_events.\n\n**Permission contract:** Explicit resource/purpose/scope/duration grant plus current task authority; rank, token balance and repository branch protections do not create confidentiality.\n\n**State/effect contract:** Desired grant state and observed provider rights reconciled by generation; independent rights preserved; expired/revoked access cleaned up with incidents visible.\n\n**Adverse/recovery cases:** Guessed object/download; high-rank holder denied; folder secrecy claim rejected; stale grant revive attempt; failed revoke; source grant removal preserves valid target grant.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.\n\n- [ ] **T081-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **T081-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **T081-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **T081-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **T081-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **T081-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **T081-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **T081-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **T081-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **T081-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T081-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T081-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T081-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T081-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T081-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **T081-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **T081-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **T081-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **T081-A01 (task acceptance)**: Every listed scenario has actual result and artifact\n- [ ] **T081-A02 (task acceptance)**: Mocks cannot replace concurrency/program/effective-access/restore evidence\n- [ ] **T081-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Read each listed AC required result\n- [ ] **T081-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Use real DB/program/provider/sandbox boundary where the scenario requires it\n- [ ] **T081-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Record candidate SHA, fixture/network, command/result and fix/retest for failures\n\n- [ ] **T081-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T081-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T081-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T081-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **T089-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **T089-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **T089-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **T089-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **T089-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **T089-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T089-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T089-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T089-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T089-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T089-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **T089-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **T089-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **T089-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **T089-A01 (task acceptance)**: Malformed/unauthorized or stale-version write is rejected consistently\n- [ ] **T089-A02 (task acceptance)**: Paginated public/private endpoints retain their actual field boundaries\n- [ ] **T089-A03 (task acceptance)**: Client eligibility or hidden buttons never grant authority\n- [ ] **T089-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Implement runtime validated /api/v1 contracts or record approved compatibility representation\n- [ ] **T089-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Use exact amount strings, UTC timestamps, cursor pagination, structured errors and revision/If-Match checks\n- [ ] **T089-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Route server actions through domain commands; protect cookie writes against CSRF/origin and service credentials against replay\n- [ ] **T089-W04 (implementation outcome)**: Prohibit generic setPaid/setRank/setState mutation routes\n\n- [ ] **T089-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T089-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T089-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T089-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI matrix](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-ci-plan.md)\n\n### Systems and subsection contracts\n\n- [00.1 — What this file is unavailable safe recovery; rollback after irreversible external effect.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. client signatures alone prove no funding.\n\n**State/effect contract:** Agreement/funding/claim/attempt states separate; verified credit bounds paid+refunded+remaining per asset; protected committed reserves cannot be withdrawn as uncommitted funds.\n\n**Adverse/recovery cases:** Partial multi-asset deposit; same ticker different mint; refund/binding race; duplicate webhook; rebuilt claim signature; frozen transfer; partial Party payout; asset-policy change.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.\n\n- [ ] **T093-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **T093-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **T093-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **T093-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **T093-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **T093-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **T093-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **T093-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **T093-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **T093-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T093-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T093-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T093-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T093-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T093-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **T093-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **T093-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **T093-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **T093-A01 (task acceptance)**: Reward reserves cannot fund compute or promotion\n- [ ] **T093-A02 (task acceptance)**: Exact accepted quote/fees and receipts remain auditable per actual asset/currency\n- [ ] **T093-A03 (task acceptance)**: Treasury analytics never treat unrelated holder wallets as project funds\n- [ ] **T093-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Model explicit owner/authorization/category and refund terms for each of the five budgets\n- [ ] **T093-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Show contractual net reward with separate actual fee/rent payer and exact quote acceptance\n- [ ] **T093-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Add supported billing/receipt handling under O08 without assumed prices, swaps or service-credit conversion\n- [ ] **T093-W04 (implementation outcome)**: Reconcile unexpected transfer, shortfall, frozen backing and category-specific encumbrance\n\n- [ ] **T093-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T093-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T093-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T093-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI matrix](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-ci-plan.md)\n\n### Systems and subsection contracts\n\n- [13.1 — Exact product Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T095-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T095-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T095-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. 216 subsections, R/P/D/I/AC/O/G groups, native epics/children and evidence register.\n\n**Permission contract:** Product owner controls recorded policy; domain owners implement bounded contracts; independent reviewers verify evidence; no agent may manufacture approvals.\n\n**State/effect contract:** Track actual NOT_STARTED/IN_PROGRESS/IMPLEMENTED_UNVERIFIED/VERIFIED_IN_TEST/PILOT_ENABLED/PRODUCTION_ENABLED evidence; project fields are planning until proven.\n\n**Adverse/recovery cases:** Missing subsection/requirement owner; closed child with no evidence; removed criterion; weaker assertion; unresolved production gate; claimed complete product with unimplemented domain.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.\n\n- [ ] **T096-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **T096-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **T096-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **T096-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **T096-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **T096-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **T096-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **T096-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **T096-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **T096-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **T096-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **T096-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **T096-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **T096-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **T096-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **T096-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **T096-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **T096-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **T096-A01 (task acceptance)**: No numbered blueprint section/subsection is unmapped\n- [ ] **T096-A02 (task acceptance)**: All 72 acceptance scenarios have concrete verification tasks\n- [ ] **T096-A03 (task acceptance)**: Board membership, hierarchy and field values match the checked-in planning register\n- [ ] **T096-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Map all numbered sections/subsections to epics/tasks/verification/decisions/gates\n- [ ] **T096-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Verify all R/P/D/I/AC/O/G IDs are covered and developer descriptions preserve canonical meanings\n- [ ] **T096-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Check native parents/blocked-by links, weekly milestone/iteration dates and UAT responsibilities\n- [ ] **T096-W04 (implementation outcome)**: Record remaining gaps and update canonical decisions only through accepted owner instructions\n\n- [ ] **T096-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **T096-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **T096-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **T096-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI matrix](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-ci-plan.md)\n\n### Systems and subsection contracts\n\nEvery assigned subsection remains listed in the task registry and [complete canonical ownership map](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-blueprint-project-map.md). Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **U003-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **U003-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **U003-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **U003-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.\n\n- [ ] **G01-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **G01-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **G01-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **G01-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **G01-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **G01-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **G01-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **G01-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **G01-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **G01-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **G01-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **G01-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **G01-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **G01-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **G01-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **G01-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **G01-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **G01-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **G01-A01 (task acceptance)**: All required gate evidence is linked and reviewed.\n- [ ] **G01-A02 (task acceptance)**: No mock/unit-only/merge result is claimed as production assurance.\n- [ ] **G01-A03 (task acceptance)**: Unpassed dependent feature remains disabled.\n- [ ] **G01-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Collect the canonical gate evidence: Approved protocol, parameters, verified IDs, authority/fee behavior, recovery.\n- [ ] **G01-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Name tested/deployed SHA, environment/network, provider/program version and operating owner.\n- [ ] **G01-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Review meaningful adverse/recovery results and outstanding decisions.\n- [ ] **G01-W04 (implementation outcome)**: Record go/limited-go/no-go; update the evidence register and exact feature flag scope.\n\n- [ ] **G01-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **G01-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **G01-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **G01-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **G04-A01 (task acceptance)**: All required gate evidence is linked and reviewed.\n- [ ] **G04-A02 (task acceptance)**: No mock/unit-only/merge result is claimed as production assurance.\n- [ ] **G04-A03 (task acceptance)**: Unpassed dependent feature remains disabled.\n- [ ] **G04-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Collect the canonical gate evidence: Exact registry, decimals/program checks, extension policy, complete tested paths.\n- [ ] **G04-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Name tested/deployed SHA, environment/network, provider/program version and operating owner.\n- [ ] **G04-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Review meaningful adverse/recovery results and outstanding decisions.\n- [ ] **G04-W04 (implementation outcome)**: Record go/limited-go/no-go; update the evidence register and exact feature flag scope.\n\n- [ ] **G04-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **G04-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **G04-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **G04-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI
