Source requirements prevail; refresh this packet if the canonical contract changes.\n\n### Exact applicable requirements and scenarios\n\n| ID | Authority class | Required behavior | Qualification / expected result |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| I03 | INVARIANT | Every financial obligation and transfer uses integer base units and a full asset identity. |  |\n| I04 | INVARIANT | Cumulative paid, refunded, and remaining obligations never exceed verified credited funds for that asset. |  |\n| I05 | INVARIANT | A duplicate command, webhook, retry, or reconciliation pass cannot create a duplicate business outcome. |  |\n| I08 | INVARIANT | Every acceptance and financial decision refers to immutable terms and a specific submission/version. |  |\n| I09 | INVARIANT | External effects are recorded, retried, and reconciled; a database transaction cannot pretend to atomically commit GitHub and Solana. |  |\n| I10 | INVARIANT | Only authorized actors can change the underlying business state; hiding a button is not authorization. |  |\n| I11 | INVARIANT | Payout, refund, access grant, and dispute decisions have an audit trail and explicit authority. |  |\n| I12 | INVARIANT | Sample program IDs, fake mints, and fabricated performance data cannot pass production validation. |  |\n| P05 | DIRECTION | Rewards can combine supported stablecoins, SOL, project tokens, and RAID. | Support follows tested adapters; “anything” is not unchecked arbitrary-token acceptance. |\n\n### Explicit domain binding — Escrow, assets and settlement\n\n**Affected canonical records:** assets, reward_obligations, escrow_agreements, funding_observations, settlement_allocations, claims, ledger_entries, chain_operations, transaction_attempts.\n\n**Permission contract:** Funder, allowed beneficiaries, allocation authority and claim authority follow accepted terms and chosen escrow contract; client signatures alone prove no funding.\n\n**State/effect contract:** Agreement/funding/claim/attempt states separate; verified credit bounds paid+refunded+remaining per asset; protected committed reserves cannot be withdrawn as uncommitted funds.\n\n**Adverse/recovery cases:** Partial multi-asset deposit; same ticker different mint; refund/binding race; duplicate webhook; rebuilt claim signature; frozen transfer; partial Party payout; asset-policy change.\n\nThese are intended contracts. Inspect actual source/migrations; implement the assigned task slice and record any remaining epic gaps.\n\n\n### Owner-required TDD, adapters and reuse\n\n| ID | Authority | Required behavior | Expected result / context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R15 | LOCKED | Every external integration is isolated behind a stable, versioned, replaceable adapter contract; provider-specific SDKs, credentials and behavior do not leak into domain rules. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| R16 | LOCKED | Every delivered module has complete current documentation, explicit dependency/host contracts and a verified consuming example so it can be reused in another authorized project. | C14; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| I13 | INVARIANT | Implementation changes follow genuine failing-test-first RED, GREEN and REFACTOR evidence; tests cannot be weakened to bypass requirements. Non-code deliverables define acceptance before execution. | C13; owner instruction 6 October 2026 |\n| AC73 | ACCEPTANCE | Replace a selected integration adapter with a contract-compatible alternate while work and external operations exist. | Same domain outcomes and typed errors; capability gaps fail closed; accepted asset/terms/authority and in-flight semantic operation/provider bindings remain intact; no duplicate effect. |\n| AC74 | ACCEPTANCE | Consume a delivered module in an independent minimal host using its published interface and documentation. | Example and contract tests run with explicit config/dependencies; no hidden RAID app state, global credentials or undeclared import; permissions, exact amounts, lifecycle and failure behavior remain enforced. |\n| AC75 | ACCEPTANCE | Submit implementation completion with missing failing-test-first, passing test, regression or independent criterion evidence. | Completion validation rejects the packet; missing/unexecuted evidence is not a PASS, and self-approval cannot satisfy independent review. |\n\n### Individually reviewable criteria\n\nEach criterion needs an actual PASS or reviewer-accepted NOT APPLICABLE rationale. FAIL, BLOCKED, missing evidence, and unexecuted checks prevent valid completion.\n\n- [ ] **G04-C01 (scope)**: State the observable user outcome, assigned milestone, in-scope commands and explicit adjacent work excluded. Compare the actual baseline to the desired behavior; identify existing working behavior that must survive.\n- [ ] **G04-C02 (authority)**: List every applicable LOCKED, DIRECTION, DEFAULT, OPEN and EXAMPLE reference separately. Keep unresolved dependent production actions disabled. A recorded owner decision must identify who accepted it, date, changed contract and effect on old accepted work.\n- [ ] **G04-C03 (entities)**: List affected canonical entities, concrete tables/models, identifiers, foreign keys, tenant scope, uniqueness and immutable fields. Identify the shared contract owner and reuse existing contracts. Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **G04-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **G04-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **G04-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **G04-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **G04-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **G04-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **G04-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **G04-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **G04-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **G04-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **G04-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **G04-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **G04-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **G04-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **G04-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **G04-A01 (task acceptance)**: All required gate evidence is linked and reviewed.\n- [ ] **G04-A02 (task acceptance)**: No mock/unit-only/merge result is claimed as production assurance.\n- [ ] **G04-A03 (task acceptance)**: Unpassed dependent feature remains disabled.\n- [ ] **G04-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Collect the canonical gate evidence: Exact registry, decimals/program checks, extension policy, complete tested paths.\n- [ ] **G04-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Name tested/deployed SHA, environment/network, provider/program version and operating owner.\n- [ ] **G04-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Review meaningful adverse/recovery results and outstanding decisions.\n- [ ] **G04-W04 (implementation outcome)**: Record go/limited-go/no-go; update the evidence register and exact feature flag scope.\n\n- [ ] **G04-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **G04-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **G04-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **G04-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI Prove database uniqueness, all-or-none Party reservations, same-engagement operator accounting, current eligibility rechecks, lock order and engagement-scoped release where touched.\n- [ ] **G07-C07 (terms-consent)**: Identify exact immutable terms, roster, payout split, beneficiary, rubric and submission version. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **G07-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. If so specify network/kind/mint/program/decimals, integer base units, verified funds, reserves, allocations, fees, claims, refunds and conservation per asset. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **G07-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **G07-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **G07-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **G07-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Do not hold database locks during provider/LLM/wallet/finality waits. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **G07-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. Verify keyboard/focus, mobile, draft preservation, exact amounts and intelligible eligibility reasons.\n- [ ] **G07-C14 (security)**: Identify applicable input validation, session/nonce/CSRF/origin, rate limit, upload quarantine, SSRF/redirect, secrets, malicious build and prompt-injection boundaries. Untrusted code and model output cannot inherit credentials, grant permissions, self-approve or expand spending.\n- [ ] **G07-C15 (operations)**: Record feature flags at server and UI, monitoring, named case owner, incident/runbook and feature-specific G01–G10 evidence. Disabling new work must preserve old claims, cancellation, dispute and access cleanup. Define migration/backfill, verified backup/restore and rollback constraints.\n- [ ] **G07-C16 (verification)**: For each requirement and criterion provide setup/fixtures, exact action, expected result, observed result, command/test, SHA, environment/network/provider version and sanitized evidence. Record failed, blocked or not-run checks accurately; compiler success is insufficient.\n- [ ] **G07-C17 (uat)**: For affected user-facing release scope identify representative journey, tester, candidate environment/SHA, expected results, defect disposition/retest and separate business sign-off. QA, UAT and release approval cannot be inferred from each other.\n- [ ] **G07-C18 (handoff)**: Record actual files, schema/API/event changes, tests executed/results, unresolved risks, authority/privacy/money effects, migration/rollback limits, reviewer and exact next bounded task. Unimplemented criteria cannot disappear through issue closure or epic roll-up.\n- [ ] **G07-A01 (task acceptance)**: All required gate evidence is linked and reviewed.\n- [ ] **G07-A02 (task acceptance)**: No mock/unit-only/merge result is claimed as production assurance.\n- [ ] **G07-A03 (task acceptance)**: Unpassed dependent feature remains disabled.\n- [ ] **G07-W01 (implementation outcome)**: Collect the canonical gate evidence: Operator identity, sandbox, tool authority, spend controls, provider data policy.\n- [ ] **G07-W02 (implementation outcome)**: Name tested/deployed SHA, environment/network, provider/program version and operating owner.\n- [ ] **G07-W03 (implementation outcome)**: Review meaningful adverse/recovery results and outstanding decisions.\n- [ ] **G07-W04 (implementation outcome)**: Record go/limited-go/no-go; update the evidence register and exact feature flag scope.\n\n- [ ] **G07-C19 (test-driven development)**: For every implementation change, define behavior from canonical requirements and write a meaningful failing test BEFORE implementation. Record RED command, actual failure and unchanged baseline; implement the smallest complete behavior; record GREEN result; refactor without changing the contract and record relevant regression results. Use real database/program/provider boundaries for material races and financial/access effects. Tests cannot be weakened, deleted or replaced with mocks merely to obtain green. For existing verified behavior, run and record the baseline and add a failing test for each changed/missing behavior; do not fabricate a red result. For decisions/docs/UAT-only work, define expected acceptance results before execution, record why a coding cycle is not applicable, and validate the actual deliverable.\n\n- [ ] **G07-C20 (replaceable integrations)**: Declare the stable versioned port, operations/capabilities, injected configuration, typed errors, cancellation/retry/idempotency, secrets, observations and provider-specific adapter boundary. Write shared contract tests first and demonstrate an alternate/test adapter without changing domain commands. Negative capability tests fail closed. Pin/reconcile in-flight operations before switching; verify no duplicate effects, asset/authority/terms drift or lost receipts. Document switch/drain/rollback and repeat affected live gates. See R15, AC73 and section 24.6.\n\n- [ ] **G07-C21 (documented independent reuse)**: Deliver module purpose/non-goals, public API/schema/event/error contracts, dependencies/host wiring, configuration, permissions, entity/state ownership, architecture, installation, runnable consuming example, tests/fixtures, limitations, migration/versioning and operations/recovery notes in the implementation change. Run the independently declared consuming host and negative/contract tests; no hidden RAID singleton/global secret or undeclared app import. Document UI accessibility and host authority when relevant. See R16, AC74 and section 24.7.\n\n- [ ] **G07-C22 (complete continuous integration coverage)**: Define the task’s unit, adapter contract/substitution, real DB/program concurrency, permissions/private-data, money properties, retry/recovery, browser/accessibility, docs/consuming-host and UAT requirements before coding. Implement meaningful tests first and wire every automated test into the owned CI suite. CI must run against the exact candidate SHA; record named checks, artifacts, actual executed/skipped counts and failures. New tests cannot be left outside CI discovery. Missing domain tests or skipped required jobs block the affected feature; mock/unit success cannot replace real races/provider or live gates. Use the feature CI matrix and independent aggregate gate; never use continue-on-error or blanket skip/allowlisting to hide failure.\n\n[Feature-by-feature CI matrix](https://github.com/solana-hackathon-1/useRAID.fun/blob/main/docs/raid-ci-plan.md)\n\n### Systems and subsection contracts\n\n- [07.1 — Account Do not assert the intended blueprint tables already exist.\n- [ ] **G10-C04 (permissions)**: Provide an actor × action × resource × state matrix for every changed read/write. Cover unauthenticated, wrong Guild, token-holder-only, self-review, expired/revoked grant and restricted account cases. Deny at the server/resource boundary; include direct API/download tests.\n- [ ] **G10-C05 (transitions)**: Provide before-state, command, authorized actor, terms/submission version, precondition, atomic mutation, after-state and rejected alternatives. Keep listing, offer, work, access, funding, settlement, dispute and run states separate. Specify finite deadlines and material cancellation/timeout paths.\n- [ ] **G10-C06 (identity-capacity)**: Use canonical participant identity across linked wallets and Guilds. Identify whether this action consumes capacity under section 13. Test stale version and unauthorized amendment. Material accepted-work changes require affected consent, valid additional funding and audit; defaults cannot rewrite old agreements.\n- [ ] **G10-C08 (money)**: Declare whether financial obligations are touched. Verify actual effects/finality and beneficiary authority; transaction submission and ticker text prove nothing.\n- [ ] **G10-C09 (privacy-access)**: Enumerate public and private DTOs, HTML hydration, metadata, search, previews, artifacts, logs and notification fields. Test absence of private bytes and effective scoped provider access. Distinguish desired from observed grants; preserve independent rights and surface failed revocation.\n- [ ] **G10-C10 (idempotency)**: Specify command identity, request digest, immutable receipt, semantic external operation and outbox/inbox deduplication. Same key plus different payload must conflict. Retry or rebuilt transaction cannot repeat business effects. Preserve intent across process crashes.\n- [ ] **G10-C11 (concurrency)**: Name every competing command and linearization boundary. Exercise meaningful independent transactions/provider boundaries for applicable acceptance, refund, claim/appeal, Party, Challenge handoff, delayed cleanup and stale job races. Record winning state and losing response; in-memory mocks do not prove database/program races.\n- [ ] **G10-C12 (external-recovery)**: List every provider/program effect, authority, generation, timeout, partial success, stale success and compensation path. Reconcile before retrying an unknown outcome; stale success cannot reopen work or grant access.\n- [ ] **G10-C13 (experience)**: Cover loading, empty, unknown/stale, validation failure, conflict, permission denied, rejected signature, pending/failed/partial effect, cancellation and recovery states where applicable. +    return participant?.id ?? null;
+  }
+  if (
+    !owner.id ||
+    !InternalId.safeParse(owner.id).success ||
+    !participant ||
+    owner.participantId !== participant.id ||
+    !['ACTIVE', 'REVOKED'].includes(owner.status ?? '') ||
+    (owner.status === 'REVOKED') !== (owner.revokedAt !== null) ||
+    (owner.revokedAt !== null && !UtcTimestamp.safeParse(owner.revokedAt).success)
+  )
+    return fail('STORAGE_CONTRACT');
+  if (owner.networkIdentity !== networkIdentity) return fail('UNSUPPORTED_IDENTITY');
+  return participant.id;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Internal ownership context under transaction-held locks; it is not proof or authorization.
+ * The host verifies a fresh sign-in proof and creates any session inside this SAME transaction.
+ * No mapping is provisioned. PRIMARY may legitimately have a null participant. ACTIVE links
+ * must reference this account's immutable HUMAN participant. Never expose this context publicly.
+ */
+export async function resolveWalletCredential(
+  tx: IdentityTransaction,
+  input: ResolveWalletCredentialInput,
+): Promise<WalletCredentialContext> {
+  const subject = credentialSubject(input);
+  validPort(tx);
+  try {
+    await query(tx, SUBJECT_LOCK, [`wallet-subject:${subject.address}`]);
+    const observed = await credentialOwner(tx, subject.address);
+    if (!observed) return { source: 'ABSENT' };
+    await lockedAccount(tx, observed.accountId);
+    // Legacy merge can reassign a PRIMARY userId without taking the subject lock. Never return
+    // an account chosen from an observation that changed while acquiring its account lock.
+    const owner = await credentialOwner(tx, subject.address);
+    if (!owner || owner.accountId !== observed.accountId) return fail('IDENTITY_CONFLICT');
+    const participantId = await credentialMapping(tx, owner, subject.networkIdentity);
+    if (owner.status === 'REVOKED') return fail('IDENTITY_REVOKED');
+    return Object.freeze({
+      source: owner.source,
+      accountId: owner.accountId,
+      participantId,
+      linkId: owner.id,
+      ...subject,
+    });
+  } catch (error) {
+    throw translate(error);
+  }
+}
+/**
+ * Revoke only an additional credential of a host-authenticated active self-session. The host
+ * owns durable audit and session invalidation in this same transaction before acknowledgement.
+ * No provider/X/primary-wallet or financial record changes and no address release/reactivation.
+ */
+export async function revokeWalletCredential(
+  tx: IdentityTransaction,
+  input: RevokeWalletCredentialInput,
+): Promise<RevokeWalletCredentialResult> {
+  validId(input?.accountId);
+  validId(input?.actorAccountId);
+  validId(input?.requestId);
+  if (input.accountId !== input.actorAccountId) return fail('WRONG_ACTOR');
+  const subject = credentialSubject(input);
+  const session = SessionSchema.safeParse(input.session);
+  const now = UtcTimestamp.safeParse(input.now);
+  if (!session.success || !now.success) return fail('INVALID_INPUT');
+  if (session.data.accountId !== input.accountId) return fail('FORBIDDEN');
+  if (session.data.state !== 'ACTIVE' || Date.parse(session.data.expiresAt) <= Date.parse(now.data))
+    return fail('AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED');
+  validPort(tx);
+  try {
+    await query(tx, SUBJECT_LOCK, [`wallet-subject:${subject.address}`]);
+    await lockedAccount(tx, input.accountId);
+    const owner = await credentialOwner(tx, subject.address);
+    if (!owner || owner.accountId !== input.accountId) return fail('IDENTITY_CONFLICT');
+    const participantId = await credentialMapping(tx, owner, subject.networkIdentity);
+    if (owner.source === 'PRIMARY') return fail('PRIMARY_WALLET_PROTECTED');
+    if (!participantId || !owner.id) return fail('STORAGE_CONTRACT');
+    if (owner.status === 'REVOKED')
+      return Object.freeze({
+        outcome: 'ALREADY_REVOKED',
+        linkId: owner.id,
+        participantId,
+        ...subject,
+        status: 'REVOKED',
+        revokedAt: owner.revokedAt!,
+      });
+    const updated = single(
+      z.strictObject({ id: z.string(), revokedAt: UtcTimestamp }),
+      await query(
+        tx,
+        `UPDATE "WalletLink" SET "status" = 'REVOKED', "revokedAt" = $3::timestamptz
+WHERE "address" = $1 AND "accountId" = $2 AND "status" = 'ACTIVE'
+RETURNING "id"::text, to_char("revokedAt" AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') AS "revokedAt"`,
+        [subject.address, input.accountId, now.data],
+      ),
+    );
+    if (!updated || updated.id !== owner.id) return fail('STORAGE_CONTRACT');
+    return Object.freeze({
+      outcome: 'REVOKED',
+      linkId: owner.id,
+      participantId,
+      ...subject,
+      status: 'REVOKED',
+      revokedAt: updated.revokedAt,
+    });
+  } catch (error) {
+    throw translate(error);
+  }
+}

+// Linearization boundary for linking (owner clarification 2026-10-10): the CURRENT session must be
+// the caller's own, live by the database clock, and carry X authority (via === 'x'), on an account
+// whose X connection still exists. Read after the subject/account locks and row-locked FOR SHARE

+// seen, and one arriving later waits for this commit (an already-decided link is not undone).
+async function observeLinkAuthority(
+  tx: Prisma.TransactionClient,
+  userId: string,
+  sessionHash: string | undefined,
+) {
+  const [session] = sessionHash
+    ? await tx.$queryRaw<{ userId: string; via: string; expiresAt: Date; now: Date }[]>`
+        SELECT "userId", "via", "expiresAt", clock_timestamp() AS "now"
+        FROM "Session" WHERE "tokenHash" = ${sessionHash} FOR SHARE`
+    : [];
+  if (!session || session.userId !== userId || session.expiresAt <= session.now)
+    throw new IdentityLinkError('AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED');
+  if (session.via !== 'x') throw new IdentityLinkError('FORBIDDEN');
+  const x = await tx.$queryRaw<{ one: number }[]>`
+    SELECT 1 AS "one" FROM "XAccount" WHERE "userId" = ${userId} FOR SHARE`;
+  if (x.length !== 1) throw new IdentityLinkError('FORBIDDEN');
+  return {
+    session: {
+      accountId: session.userId,
+      state: 'ACTIVE',
+      expiresAt: session.expiresAt.toISOString(),
+    },
+    now: session.now.toISOString(),
+  };
+}
+function linkFailure(error: unknown): HttpError | null {
+  if (!(error instanceof IdentityLinkError)) return null;
+  const [status, message] = LINK_HTTP[error.code] ?? [503, 'Wallet linking is unavailable.'];
+  return new HttpError(status, message);
+}
+// Adds a sign-in wallet to the caller's own account. The payout wallet never changes. Requires the
+// server switch, a connected X account, the caller's own live session read here (never client
+// asserted) and a fresh single-use proof from the additional wallet.
+export async function linkAdditionalWallet(
+  userId: string,
+  digest: string,
+  signature: string,
+  address: string,
+  currentSessionHash: string | undefined,
+  requestId: string,
+): Promise<PublicWalletLink> {
+  if (!walletLinksEnabled()) throw new HttpError(400, 'Invalid wallet challenge.');
+  walletAddress(address);
+  const bytes = decodeSignature(signature);
+  const url = new URL(config.appUrl);
+  try {
+    const linked = await db.$transaction(
+      async (tx) => {
+        const attempt = await consumeChallenge(
+          tx,
+          digest,
+          address,
+          bytes,
+          userId,
+          'link-additional',
+        );
+        return linkVerifiedWallet(createPrismaIdentityTransaction(tx), {
+          accountId: userId,
+          actorAccountId: userId,
+          requestId,
+          subject: { networkIdentity: SIWS_CHAIN_ID, address },
+          proof: deriveWalletLinkProof(attempt, { signatureVerified: true }),
+          // Authority is observed by the module under the subject and account locks (below).
+          observeAuthority: () => observeLinkAuthority(tx, userId, currentSessionHash),
+          policy: {
+            domain: url.host,
+            uri: url.origin,
+            walletNetworks: [SIWS_CHAIN_ID],
+            providers: [],
+          },
+          limits: LINK_LIMITS,
+        });
       },
-    });
-  });
+      { isolationLevel: Prisma.TransactionIsolationLevel.ReadCommitted },
+    );
+    return publicWalletLink(linked);
+  } catch (error) {
+    throw linkFailure(error) ?? error;
+  }
 }
